description:
FILED s473t5d (Opus, 2026-09-13) by #1501 round 5 CHECK 1.

t/io/dup.t aborts at its line 68 with

  Cannot dup to string '1': Bad file descriptor

and the whole rest of the file (19 of perl's 29 rows) is lost.  The abort is
NOT about the string '1' -- `%p-open-dup` parses a numeric fd string fine.  It
is that descriptor 1 IS ALREADY CLOSED by then, by the file's own line 65:

  open(F,">&=",1) or die; print F "ok 11\n"; close(F);

`>&=` is fdopen: the new handle IS descriptor 1.  PCL builds an fd-stream over
it, and `close(F)` closes the stream, which closes descriptor 1 -- taking
STDOUT with it ("Couldn't write to #<fd-stream for descriptor 1>: Bad file
descriptor" in the exit hook).

PERL DOES NOT (probed 5.40.3, both on a std fd and on a plain file):
  open(F, ">&=", 1); print F "A\n"; close(F);
  open(G, ">&=", '1');        -> SUCCEEDS in perl, EBADF in PCL
  print STDOUT "C\n";         -> prints in perl, lost in PCL
  # and on a file: fdopen a second handle over fileno($o), close it, then
  # print $o -- perl writes BOTH lines into the file.
So the observable rule is: CLOSING AN `=`-FORM (fdopen) HANDLE RELEASES THE
HANDLE, NOT THE DESCRIPTOR.

FIX SHAPE: in `%p-open-dup`, the eq-form branch that builds a fresh stream over
`src-fd` (the raw-fd-number case -- the "share the stream object" case is
already right) must produce a stream whose `close` does not close the fd.  CL
`close` on an fd-stream always closes the descriptor, so this needs a registry
of fdopen ALIAS streams that `%p-close`/`%p-close-maybe-pipe` consult: flush
(`finish-output`), forget the handle, answer perl's true, and DO NOT close.
`make-fd-stream`'s `:auto-close` defaults to NIL, so an unclosed alias stream
does not get a finalizer that would close the fd later.

Probe the case it would BREAK: `>&` (a real dup) must still close its own
descriptor; a `>&=` over a handle PCL already has a stream for must keep
sharing that stream object (task #592's FD_CLOEXEC note is the same branch);
and `close` must still reap a fork-pipe child.

ROWS: t/io/dup.t 20 blessed fail rows (17 of them `ok -> (missing)`) +
19 shortfall.
subject: closing a `>&=` (fdopen) handle CLOSES the shared descriptor, where perl leaves it open -- t/io/dup.t loses 19 rows and STDOUT itself dies mid-file
